subject: FIVS
title: Forensic Implications of Inheritance
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Forensic genetics with an emphasis on basic principles of genetics/inheritance, linkage/recombination, mutation, population genetics, gene expression and genetic application in the forensic sciences; development, use and evaluation of forensically relevant molecular markers along with modern sequencing techniques/databases. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in BIOL 112 ; FIVS-SCE and FIVS-LWE majors; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in BIOL 112 ; FIVS-SCE and FIVS-LWE majors; junior or senior classification.

subject: FIVS
title: Forensic Molecular Biology
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. This course is designed to illustrate the use of a variety of molecular biology methods for forensic applications. The core elements that will be covered include prokaryotic and eukaryotic genome structure and function; interrelationship of DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis; transcription, translation, replication; gene expression and regulation; recombinant DNA techniques; PCR; and DNA sequencing. Students will gain an appreciation and understanding of the underlying molecular biology techniques that are used in a diverse array of settings, including blood analysis, blood typing, DNA fingerprinting and genetic testing. The potential future use of advanced sequencing technologies for forensic and other applications will be discussed. Additionally, the social, ethical and legal implications of these procedures and applications will be fully considered. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 308 ; FIVS-SCE majors.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in FIVS 308 ; FIVS-SCE majors.

subject: FIVS
title: /FSTC 319 Molecular Microbial Detection and Characterization
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. The overall objective of this course is to provide students from different disciplinary interests with the knowledge and hands-on skills in specific molecular microbial detection and characterization methods employed in the food and fermentation industries, environmental and other natural and man-made environments. The course will expose students to the fundamentals of microbial pathogen detection and associated molecular methods and provide a basis on how detection methods should be used for the different applications. The students will learn how to apply these methods in different scenarios and applications and how to interpret the results from such methods. Prerequisites: BIOL 111 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: FSTC 319/FIVS 319 .
prereq_text: BIOL 111 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: FIVS
title: Impression Evidence
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Individual and class characteristics of footwear, tire track, impression evidence documentation, collection, test impression techniques, shoe and tire tread designs, sizing, manufacturing, wear characteristics, comparison techniques, courtroom preparation and testimony. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 205 and FIVS 210 ; FIVS majors.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in FIVS 205 and FIVS 210 ; FIVS majors.

subject: FIVS
title: /SCSC 401 Forensic Soil Science
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Examination of soils physical attributes, mineralogy, chemistry and microbiology to solve crimes; soil and geologic characteristics associated with crime scene examination; physical, chemical and biological characteristics and use of trace evidence. Statistical methods used in evidence comparison. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in FIVS 282 . Cross Listing: SCSC 401/FIVS 401 .
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in FIVS 282 .

subject: FIVS
title: /CYBR 405 Applied Digital Forensics and Incident Response
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Collection of digital evidence; digital evidence analytics; analysis of log data; malware triage; recover damaged digital evidence; write technical reports on malware and incidents; legal and ethical components of digital forensic science. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: CYBR 405/FIVS 405 .
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

subject: FIVS
title: Advanced Cyberforensics
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. The course is designed to equip students with the technical and analytical skills required to investigate complex cyber incidents, recover critical evidence and analyze sophisticated threats in digital environments. The course covers a comprehensive range of topics, including Windows and memory forensics, network forensics, incident response (IR), threat hunting, intrusion analysis, malware analysis, mobile forensics and emerging technologies such as IoT, SCADA and AI. Through hands-on exercises and theoretical instruction, the course prepares students to address advanced adversarial tactics and produce actionable forensic findings in real-world scenarios. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 405/CYBR 405 ; FIVS majors; junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in FIVS 405/CYBR 405 ; FIVS majors; junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

subject: FIVS
title: Practice and Principles of Science and Law
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Introduction to series of practitioners of forensic science and the justice system; receive instruction on principles, procedures, and practices used in solving legal and societal issues; examine scientific method and scientific knowledge as applied through expert testimony; enhance critical thinking and reasoning skills in studying and debating different positions of current issues of science and law. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 205 and FIVS 481 ; grade of C or better in FIVS 316 and FIVS 435 , or concurrent enrollment; FIVS-LWE and FIVS-SCE majors.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in FIVS 205 and FIVS 481 ; grade of C or better in FIVS 316 and FIVS 435 , or concurrent enrollment; FIVS-LWE and FIVS-SCE majors.

Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 308 or concurrent enrollment; FIVS-LWE and FIVS-SCE majors.

description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Examination of principles, procedures and methodologies used in crime scene investigation; instruction in scene documentation, evidence recognition and collection protocols; application of forensic techniques, including photography, sketching and trace recovery, within simulated scenarios that emphasize critical thinking, professional standards and defensible decision-making in investigative contexts. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in FIVS 205 or concurrent enrollment; FIVS-LWE and FIVS-SCE majors.

title: /ENTO 431 The Science of Forensic Entomology
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Explores the science, methodology and technology employed to gather, preserve and present information about insects and other arthropods in such a manner that this information can be used in courts of law as evidence and testimony to help resolve issues of a criminal or civil nature. description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview of the interdisciplinary field of wildlife forensics; application of scientific techniques to the investigation of wildlife crimes; exploration of the methods used to identify illegal activities such as poaching, wildlife trafficking, and habitat destruction; forensic techniques in species identification, genetics, DNA analysis, and trace evidence collection; exploration of legal framework surrounding wildlife crime; practical applications of forensic science to conservation and biodiversity protection. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; ECCB 406 or GEOG 462 recommended. Cross Listing: ECCB 434/FIVS 434 .

subject: GEOG
title: Geography of the United States
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. This systematic and regional course introduces geographic issues covering the geography of the United States from environmental, political, social/cultural and economic perspectives with a focus on the many ways that culture, politics, economics and social difference are manifested in and through spatial relations and processes. Our case studies will emphasize that the United States is an ever-changing configuration of ideas, institutions, people and objects. This course also aims to develop conceptual tools for critical thinking, rather than an encyclopedic knowledge of the United States’ geographic features. Finally, the course introduces students to a variety of concepts and methods that geographers use to analyze spatial patterns and processes. subject: GEOG
title: Environmental Justice
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. This course examines the uneven distribution of environmental benefits and burdens across society, drawing on the scholarly literature referred to as environmental justice research. You will examine historical and contemporary evidence for disparities in exposure to environmental hazards, including but not limited to air and water pollution, as well as disparities in access to environmental amenities, including but not limited to urban greenspace. Topics address variation in environmental conditions and policy outcomes across different demographic and geographic contexts, including those associated with race, gender, ethnicity and class, as these social categories are used in empirical research and policy analysis. The course treats these social categories as analytical descriptors rather than normative or ideological claims. Content includes controversial and contested scholarly perspectives on environmental issues, reflecting multiple explanatory frameworks for understanding the causes of and proposed policy responses to uneven environmental distributions. Drawing on readings from a range of disciplines, such as environmental science, geography and urban planning, you will evaluate proposed explanations for observed patterns, including but not limited to market dynamics, land-use decisions, regulatory enforcement, historical settlement patterns and institutional decision-making processes. You will also compare policy and governance responses discussed in the scholarly literature, such as market-based mechanisms, participatory decision-making arrangements and strengthened regulatory oversight, assessing their assumptions, empirical support and trade-offs. The course emphasizes evidence-based reasoning and civil discourse, preparing you to engage constructively with contentious environmental policy contexts. An independent research project will train you to develop and defend an analytical argument related to an environmental justice issue of your choosing using appropriate evidence. Throughout the course, your work will be evaluated on the quality of analysis and reasoning, not on agreement with any particular political, moral or ideological position. Prerequisites: GEOG 201 or GEOG 202 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: GEOL
title: Economic Geology
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Formation, distribution and geological occurrences of ore deposits. Topics include a review of mineralogy with an emphasis on ore minerals (important examples include sulfide and oxide ore minerals); igneous petrology with an emphasis on ore-forming igneous processes such as fractional crystallization, magma mixing and liquid immiscibility; ore-forming fluids, fluid-rock interaction and the generation of hydrothermal ore deposits; sedimentology with an emphasis on low-temperature fluids (e.g., ocean water), oxidation-reduction reactions and the formation of ore deposits hosted in sedimentary rocks (e.g., banded iron formations); weathering of rocks and the formation of bauxite and similar ore deposits. These topics will be covered in conjunction with the broader topic of plate tectonics and its control over the geographic distribution of ore deposits, as well as the economic and environmental impact of mineral exploitation. Prerequisites: GEOL 203 ; GEOL 101 and GEOL 102 , or GEOL 104 , or GEOL 150 ; CHEM 119 , or CHEM 107 and CHEM 117 or concurrent enrollment.

title: Seminar
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. CONTENT. Capstone seminar. Instructors select different topics and assign distinct readings to meet the learning objectives. All sections include the use of primary source materials related to the topic of the seminar; problems of bibliography, historiography and historical method; scholarship concerning a particular issue, event, period or people in history; and instruction and experience in historical writing. Course content is selected to align with the course description and the current state of scholarship in the field. The presentation of course content fosters critical thinking in the context of scholarly consensus and debate, rather than instructors’ views, values or beliefs. BENEFITS. History teaches evaluation and synthesis of evidence, development of persuasive arguments in written and oral form, expansion of understandings of historical contexts that have contributed to human complexity past and present, including but not limited to the formation of group and individual identities, social and political dynamics, and debates about values and rights. Applying this knowledge produces more informed citizens, who are proficient in the abilities required by today’s workforce. May be repeated for credit. Information and communication technologies in the hospitality, tourism, recreation, and event management fields; analysis of technology adoption and how technology is used for knowledge management, support, collaboration, communication, accounting, reservations and scheduling, forecasting, and payments. Prerequisites: HMGT 211 and HMGT 223 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 211 and HMGT 223 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Tourism Capstone
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Application of theoretical frameworks and tourism management concepts to a project with a participating company; strategic analysis of company structure and needs; research of areas and markets; analysis and presentation of findings in accordance with project objectives. Prerequisites: HMGT 302 ; HMGT 320 or HMGT 446 ; HMGT 401 ; senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 302 ; HMGT 320 or HMGT 446 ; HMGT 401 ; senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Financing Hospitality, Hotel, and Tourism Services
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Exploration of financial vehicles for funding hospitality, hotels and tourism organizations and services. Prerequisites: HMGT 223 or HMGT 411 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 223 or HMGT 411 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Law, Negotiation, and Risk Management in Hospitality, Tourism and Recreation
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Evaluation of laws and lines of legal inquiry related to work in hospitality, events, tourism, youth, and recreation settings; skills related to contract negotiation and review; elements of contracts and completion of agreements. Prerequisites: HMGT 201 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 201 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Strategic Management for Hospitality and Tourism
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Fundamentals of strategic management in hospitality and tourism contexts using theoretical frameworks and practical applications; three phases in the strategic management process – planning, implementation and evaluation will be examined; critical evaluations of the long-term strategic issues affecting hospitality and tourism enterprises. Prerequisites: HMGT 201 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 201 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Revenue Management
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Demand-based pricing system employed in the hospitality and tourism industry coupled with information technology resulting in long term strategic impacts; role and function of revenue manager as the key executive responsible for managing the pricing and supply policies in hotels and airlines. Prerequisites: HMGT 352 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 352 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Seminar for the Visitor Economy
description: Credits 3. 3 Other Hours. Overview of micro, meso, and macro-economic effects of tourism related enterprises on the visitor economy; challenges facing managers in relation to the visitor economy, whether local, state, regional, national or global; impacts and opportunities for various tourism sectors. Prerequisites: HMGT 201 ; HMGT 223 or HMGT 411 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 201 ; HMGT 223 or HMGT 411 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Contemporary Hotel and Resort Development
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. International contemporary trends including Integrated Resort and Mega Hotels to include accommodations, entertainment, event venues, theme parks, luxury management and retail facilities; course will address branding and market segmentation, and how those specific niches influence future development of hotels and resorts. Prerequisites: HMGT 352 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 352 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Leadership for Outdoor Recreation
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Leadership principles related to outdoor recreation; classroom instruction and experiential learning; skills training through field trips; risk management planning, environmental education, group facilitation, and trip planning. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Hospitality Enterprises Practicum
description: Credits 3. 3 Other Hours. Practical experience working in a professional hospitality setting; offered on an individual basis. Prerequisites: HMGT 201 , HMGT 281 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 201 , HMGT 281 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Seminar
description: Credit 1. 1 Other Hour. Development of knowledge and skills necessary for employment in hospitality, hotel management and tourism; career preparation and job search strategies, professionalism, networking and opportunities for advanced education; preparation for internship and post-graduation positions. Prerequisites: HMGT majors; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT majors; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Internship
description: Credits 3. 3 Other Hours. Practical experience working in a professional hospitality, hotel management, tourism, event management or recreation setting; offered on an individual basis. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisites: HMGT 340 and HMGT 384 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HMGT 340 and HMGT 384 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HMGT
title: Directed Studies
description: Credits 0 to 4. 0 to 4 Other Hours. For individual research by advanced undergraduates upon a broad range of subjects not included in established courses. Prerequisite: Junior classification or approval of department head.
prereq_text: Junior classification or approval of department head.

subject: HMGT
title: Special Topics in...
description: Credits 1 to 4. 1 to 4 Lecture Hours. 0 to 9 Lab Hours. Selected topics in an identified area of hospitality, hotel, tourism, recreation and event management. May be repeated for credit.

subject: HMGT
title: Research
description: Credits 1 to 3. 1 to 3 Other Hours. Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in Hospitality, Hotel Management and Tourism. Registration in multiple sections of this course are possible within a given semester provided that the per semester credit hour limit is not exceeded. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification and approval of instructor.

subject: HONR
title: Honors Seminar in Respect, Excellence, and Leadership
description: Credit 1. 1 Lecture Hour. Seminar on Respect, Excellence, and Leadership; focus on common readings and discussion of issues of broad concern to society. Prerequisites: First-year Honors Academy.
prereq_text: First-year Honors Academy.

title: Honors Seminar in Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service
description: Credit 1. 1 Lecture Hour. Seminar on Respect, Excellence, and Leadership; focus on common readings and discussion of issues of broad concern to society. Prerequisites: Grade of B or better in HONR 101 ; first-year Honors Academy.
prereq_text: Grade of B or better in HONR 101 ; first-year Honors Academy.

subject: HONR
title: Honors Seminar in Aggie Core Values
description: Credits 2. 2 Lecture Hours. Seminar on Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service; focus on reading and discussion; open to all majors; restricted to transfer and continuing students accepted to the Honors Academy and limited in size to provide a small-class experience. Prerequisites: Acceptance to Honors Academy; Honors Minor.
prereq_text: Acceptance to Honors Academy; Honors Minor.

title: Honors Seminar in Respect
description: Credit 1. 1 Lecture Hour. subject: HONR
title: Honors Culminating Experience
description: Credits 0. 0 Other Hours. Demonstrating mastery of knowledge, skills, and abilities as applied to an original problem through an independent, mentored project; public presentation of work. Prerequisites: Honors Minor; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Honors Minor; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Horticultural Science and Practices
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. (AGRI 1315, AGRI 1415*, HORT 1301, HORT 1401*) Horticultural Science and Practices. Structure, growth and development of horticultural plants from a practical and scientific approach; environmental effects, basic principles of propagation, greenhouse and outdoor production, nutrition, pruning and chemical control of growth, pest control and branches of horticulture.

subject: HORT
title: Horticultural Science and Practices Laboratory
description: Credit 1. 3 Lab Hours. (HORT 1101, AGRI 1115, HORT 1401*, AGRI 1415*) Horticultural Science and Practices Laboratory. Methods and practices related to production of horticultural crops; practical exercises in greenhouse and field. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or concurrent enrollment.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or concurrent enrollment.

subject: HORT
title: Floral Design
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Principles of design illustrated with the use of floral materials; floral design elements and techniques including color, form, line and texture; history and utilization of floral art in society.

subject: HORT
title: Professions in Horticulture
description: Credit 1. 1 Lecture Hour. Comprehensive view of the opportunities in the science, technology and art of horticultural sciences and potential career paths; sub-disciplines by crop (fruit, vegetable, viticulture, nut, ornamental crops, floral crops, controlled environment and urban horticulture) and approach (research, technology, biotechnology, mechanization, genetics, genomics, and breeding, phenomics, landscaping, production, sustainability, floral design, indoor farming, and entrepreneurship); examination of the national and international scope and economic, environmental and health impacts of horticulture; major horticultural regions in Texas; interactions with representatives and leaders of various horticultural industries; featured horticulture innovations presented by inventors; development of an online professional profile, such as LinkedIn.

subject: HORT
title: Research
description: Credits 1 to 3. 1 to 3 Other Hours. Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in horticulture. May be repeated 2 times for credit. Prerequisites: Freshman or sophomore classification and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Freshman or sophomore classification and approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Garden Science
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Identification, propagation, soil management, fertilization, growth control and protection of common garden plants: indoor ornamentals, landscape ornamentals, fruits and vegetables; special topics include home landscaping, container gardens, bonsai, herbs and medicinal plants and hobby greenhouse management; overview of the effects of organic and non-organic practices on the garden ecosystem. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Trees and Shrubs for Sustainable Built Environments
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Better known woody ornamental trees and shrubs; identification, morphology, classification, nomenclature and adaptability for use in landscape environments. Prerequisite: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 , BIOL 113 , HORT 301 , LAND 101 , ECCB 205 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 , BIOL 113 , HORT 301 , LAND 101 , ECCB 205 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Plants for Sustainable Landscapes
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Identification and use of indigenous and introduced landscape plants; plants for special uses in urban environments; emphasis on plants' ornamental attributes, cultural requirements, and adaptability in urban and suburban environments. Prerequisite: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 , BIOL 113 , HORT 301 , LAND 101 , ECCB 205 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 , BIOL 113 , HORT 301 , LAND 101 , ECCB 205 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Interior Plants
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Identification, selection and maintenance of interior foliage plants; emphasis on design solutions for commercial and private facilities. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Introduction to Plant Physiology
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Study of principal life processes of higher plants; influence of environmental factors on these processes; agricultural and ecological significance of life processes of plants. Prerequisite: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 or BIOL 113 and CHEM 222 or CHEM 227 .
prereq_text: BIOL 101 , BIOL 111 or BIOL 113 and CHEM 222 or CHEM 227 .

subject: HORT
title: Issues in Horticulture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Analysis and exploration of factors that impinge on modern horticultural systems, including technological, environmental, economic and societal issues; emphasis on student-driven research on critical issues that affect a horticultural industry sector of interest to the student. Self-driven research is coupled with writing-intensive coursework. Prerequisites: HORT 202 ; grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: HORT 202 ; grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Fruit and Nut Production
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Rootstocks, cultivars, identification, site selection, pollination, pruning, fruit thinning, dormancy, orchard culture management, irrigation, pest control, harvesting and post harvest physiology of temperate fruit and nut species. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 .
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 .

subject: HORT
title: Vegetable Crop Production
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Origin, nutritive value, economic importance, botany and cultural practices of the major vegetable crops. Lab activities include organic and non-organic production of major vegetable crops.

subject: HORT
title: Plant Propagation
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Principles, practices and techniques followed in the sexual and asexual propagation of horticultural plants: seed technology and seed propagation, rooting and propagation of cuttings, graftage and budding systems, layering and propagation by specialized plant structures, biotechnology and tissue culture systems for micropropagation. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Wild Edible, Cultivated and Poisonous Herbs
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Identification, reported uses and cultivation of popular garden herbs, historically useful herbs and wild edible and poisonous herbs; the history of phytomedicinal herbs and the role of horticulture in the advent of select modern pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals; native Texas wild edible and culturally-useful herbs; reported uses and efficacy of essential oils of herbal plants; propagation and production of cultivated herbs and wild edible plants. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Horticulture Landscape Graphics
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Graphic representation of landscape design; demonstrations of technique; examination of drawing examples and drawing production; basic hand graphics techniques for visual-thinking and presentation-quality landscape drawings. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Sociohorticulture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Horticulture as it relates to humans through people-plant interactions; use of horticulture to improve quality of life; awareness and appreciation of the economic, environmental, social and health benefits of plants. Prerequisite: Junior classification.
prereq_text: Junior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Landscapes of Sustainable Built Environments
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Construction and maintenance considerations for landscapes in urban sustainable environments, including green roofs, bioretention cells, rain gardens, and living walls; how to maximize benefits of each system, current trends in regulatory and permitting processes of green infrastructure, and the development of industry-wide guidelines versus standards. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or concurrent enrollment, or junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or concurrent enrollment, or junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Field Studies in Horticulture
description: Credits 1 to 3. 1 to 9 Other Hours. History of garden design and the development of the field of Ornamental Horticulture; designs of famous designers Capability Brown and Gertrude Jekyll; pastoral and formal design themes; plant selection and placement from an artistic and functional design perspective; European manipulation of plant form. Prerequisites: HORT 201 or HORT 301 and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 201 or HORT 301 and approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Plant Breeding
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Application of genetics and other sciences to breeding and improvement of horticultural crops; methods and special techniques employed. Offered in even numbered years. Only one of the following will satisfy the requirements for a degree: HORT 404 or SCSC 304 . Prerequisite: SCSC 205 , GENE 302 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: SCSC 205 , GENE 302 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 , or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Hydroponic and Soilless Crop Production
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Principles, practices, and techniques exploring the science and management of controlled environment crop production using hydroponics and other soil-less cultivation methods; construction and maintenance of hydroponic systems and the growth of crops in a research and commercial production setting. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 and junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 and junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Sustainable Organic Horticulture
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Principles and practices of sustainable organic horticulture production systems; organic certification requirements, policies, and regulations; cultural practices, techniques, and marketing strategies; focus on commercial cultivation of horticultural crops. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Understanding Wine - From Vines to Wines and Beyond
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Facets of wine in the United States and around the world; the history of wine, grape growing and winemaking, types of wine, wine etiquette, beer and spirits, sensory evaluation, wine marketing, and winery tasting room and event management. Prerequisites: Must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Nut Culture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Orchard management, native grove development, cultivars, fruit setting, soils, nutrition, propagation, pest control, harvesting, shelling, storage and marketing of temperate tree nut crops grown in the U.S. with major emphasis on pecans. Offered in odd numbered years. Prerequisite: HORT 319 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 319 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Viticulture and Small Fruit Culture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Classic winegrape culture in Europe and U.S. are taught; influence of climate, soil, cultivar, rootstock, canopy and management is presented; nutrition, water, spacing, trellis, pruning, IPM and harvest are integrated for quality yields; culture of muscadines, berries, figs and persimmons are taught. Offered in even numbered years. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Concepts of Wine Production
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Classic wine grapes of the world and where they are produced; evaluation of wine style and quality through formal laboratory tastings. Prerequisites: FSTC 201 or grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: FSTC 201 or grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Enology
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Provides a basic understanding of each step of the wine making process; emphasis on home and small scale commercial wine production as related to Texas conditions. Prerequisites: Must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Must be 21 years of age; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Tropical Horticulture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Production, processing and marketing of coffee, bananas, cacao, mango, cashew, pineapple, coconut and root and tuber crops; recent significant developments in plant breeding and cultural practices. Offered in odd numbered years. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Horticulture Landscape Installation
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Principles and practices of grading, drainage and construction of residential and small commercial landscapes; cost and bid estimation; soil preparation; transplanting operations; control of landscape diseases and pests; estimating maintenance requirements of landscape installations. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: International Floriculture Marketing
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Importance, cost, and opportunities in marketing floral products, fresh cut flowers, flowering potted plants, foliage plants, and bedding/garden plants; topics include: world production areas, economic value, species grown, marketing channels, retail environments, current/future consumers, postharvest handling, promotion/advertising, perceived/added value, marketing trends and employment opportunities. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: Greenhouse Technology & Sustainable Crop Production Systems
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Greenhouse Technology & Sustainable Crop Production Systems. Technology used to operate and manage energy efficient greenhouses for sustainable production of crops; greenhouse structures, equipment and automation; heating, cooling and ventilating systems; environmental computerized controls; environmental inputs as they affect plant physiological processes and influence plant growth and development including temperature and light, root substrates, water quantity and quality, irrigation efficiency, fertilization sources and integrated pest management; sustainable crop production systems and practices for hydroponics, plug production, photoperiodic crops, vernalization and lighting technology to produce vegetative and reproductive plant products; scheduling, controlling growth, harvesting and marketing practices for commercially important, high quality, high value crops. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 and junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 and junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Floriculture Crop Production
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Production of floriculture crops in the greenhouse environment; scheduling and controlling crop growth for target market periods; specific flowering crops will be used as models to demonstrate potted flowering plant, cut flower, and garden plant production systems; hands-on crop production experience in lab. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Nursery Production and Management
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Container, field and protected culture production of ornamental nursery plants (shrubs, trees, ground covers, bedding plants and herbaceous perennials); retail and wholesale nursery-site selection and development, financing, niche-marketing, personnel and labor management; wholesale nursery production cycles and systems, storage and shipping. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in HORT 201 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Horticulture Landscape Design
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Application of the principles and elements of design to planning and developing both exterior residential landscape designs and interior commercial designs. Prerequisites: HORT 332 or concurrent enrollment; HORT 306 or concurrent enrollment, or HORT 308 ; or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 332 or concurrent enrollment; HORT 306 or concurrent enrollment, or HORT 308 ; or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Urban Horticulture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Introduction to urban horticulture and its role in community development and well-being; emphasis on career opportunities and the roles of the urban horticulture programmer. Offered in odd numbered years. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

subject: HORT
title: International Horticulture
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Examines the source of horticultural commodities; shows how geography, culture, politics, and history influence our markets, gardens and kitchens; educates students on interpreting different garden styles. Prerequisites: HORT 301 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 301 , grade of C or better in HORT 201 ; and approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Horticulture Landscape Design II
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Computer-aided-drafting (CAD) to produce site layout, grading and planting plan, and construction details for small-scale landscape design; advanced design principles and practices in their historical context, includes design and drafting of hardscape details, manipulation of earth forms, ecological urban park design to traditional garden design. Prerequisites: HORT 432 ; HORT 306 or HORT 308 , or concurrent enrollment, or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 432 ; HORT 306 or HORT 308 , or concurrent enrollment, or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Key Metabolites in Horticultural Crops
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Fundamentals of horticultural crop metabolic compounds, including secondary metabolites as they relate to plant development, nutrition, and stress responses in horticultural crops; utilization of online tools to analyze, organize, and visualize metabolite data; evaluation of organoleptic properties of the important metabolites of horticultural crops including nuts, grapes, fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamentals; critical evaluation of current topics in horticultural crop metabolic research and technology to advance scientific research; exploration of applications of horticulture metabolites in human health. Prerequisites: CHEM 119 and a grade of C or better in HORT 201 .
prereq_text: CHEM 119 and a grade of C or better in HORT 201 .

subject: HORT
title: Processing Coffee and High-Value Horticultural Crops
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Examination of the principles behind coffee processing and other high-value food crops including cultivation; different unit processing operations; methods for preservation; packaging and marketing strategies; and a processing plant visit. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Retail Floristry
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Principles of floral design in a commercial shop enterprise; aspects of design in vase arrangements, personal flowers, sympathy flowers and flowers for special occasions; production costs and profit analysis, selling techniques and customer relations; term project required. Prerequisite: HORT 203 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 203 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Floral Design: Weddings and Personal Flowers
description: Credits 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Basic principles of floral design as applied to wedding work; design principles and mechanics as applied to corsages, headpieces, hand bouquets and ceremony and reception decorations; history of wedding traditions; selling and pricing weddings. Prerequisite: HORT 203 or HORT 451 or approval of instructor.
prereq_text: HORT 203 or HORT 451 or approval of instructor.

subject: HORT
title: Floral Art

title: Global Context of Business
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Examination of how culture, government, history, politics, economy, and current events of one or more countries affect business; development of understanding of the foreign country or countries; real world comprehension on how to successfully engage in business due to understanding the economic, cultural, and political issues facing the country; global field-study based course with a duration of 1-2 weeks abroad. Prerequisite: Admitted to Mays Business School and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Admitted to Mays Business School and approval of instructor.

subject: IBUS
title: Global Sustainable Business
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Examination of sustainable business development, financial literacy, and small business consulting; real world comprehension on how to successfully engage in sustainable business development in context of host community and country's economic, cultural, and political issues; global field-study based course with hands on experience engaging indigenous, rural community for 1-2 weeks abroad. May be repeated two times for credit. Prerequisite: Admitted to Mays Business School and approval of instructor.
prereq_text: Admitted to Mays Business School and approval of instructor.

title: /MKTG 401 Global Marketing
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Survey of the aspects involved in marketing goods and services in a global marketplace; social, political, legal and economic issues associated with conducting business globally. Prerequisite: MKTG 321 . Cross Listing: MKTG 401/IBUS 401 .

title: /MKTG 402 International Marketing: Study Abroad
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Introduction to the facets of doing business in an international setting; provides exposure to a variety of foreign cultures; facilitates understanding of the international marketplace in which these students will function. Prerequisites: MKTG 321 or MKTG 409 ; junior classification; 2.5 GPR overall. Cross Listing: MKTG 402/IBUS 402 .
prereq_text: MKTG 321 or MKTG 409 ; junior classification; 2.5 GPR overall.

subject: IBUS
title: /MKTG 403 International Market Entry Strategies
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. A research-based course in which students prepare an analysis of a country, or region outside the U.S., and use it in the preparation of a marketing plan for a good or service to be introduced and marketed in that country. Prerequisites: MKTG 321 or MKTG 409 ; concurrent registration in IBUS 402/MKTG 402 or MKTG 402/IBUS 402 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: MKTG 403/IBUS 403 .
prereq_text: MKTG 321 or MKTG 409 ; concurrent registration in IBUS 402/MKTG 402 or MKTG 402/IBUS 402 ; junior or senior classification.

subject: IBUS
title: /ISTM 440 International Technology Management
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Examines global information and communications technology (ICT) business environment; challenges and opportunities for technology companies in the region; history, culture, politics, economic issues, and infrastructure influencing ICT support and innovation in the region; combination of classroom work in the spring and a field trip to the selected country in the summer; repeatable for credit if taken in a different country. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; approval of instructor. Cross Listing: ISTM 440/IBUS 440 .
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification; approval of instructor.

subject: IBUS
title: /FINC 445 International Finance
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. International business transactions, balance of payments and exchange rate systems, exchange rate risk and hedging techniques, sources of funding, relation to international financial institutions and capital instruments; foreign direct investment; international asset and liability management. Prerequisites: FINC 351 and FINC 361 ; ACCT 328 or concurrent enrollment. Cross Listing: FINC 445/IBUS 446 .
prereq_text: FINC 351 and FINC 361 ; ACCT 328 or concurrent enrollment.

subject: IBUS
title: /MGMT 450 International Environment of Business
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Broad survey of international business issues; analyzes the environment in which international businesses operate; examines international economic issues including trade theory, investment theory, foreign exchange and capital markets, and balance of payments; introduces multinational enterprises, global competition, international organizations, treaties and international law, national trade policies and the determinants of competitiveness of firms in international markets. Prerequisites: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School. Cross Listing: MGMT 450/IBUS 450 .
prereq_text: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.

subject: IBUS
title: Asian Business Environment
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. The scope of business environments of Asia; geographical, demographic and cultural makeup; economic integration; human and cultural elements; financial and communication infrastructures; risk and market analysis; trade and investment patterns; Asian MNC's. May be repeated for credit if taken in a different country. Prerequisite: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.
prereq_text: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.

subject: IBUS
title: European Integration and Business
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. History and institutional structure of the European Union; its regional cultures, values, economies and rifts; challenges faced by corporations and people in the region, including issues involving doing business with the European Union. May be repeated one time for credit. Prerequisite: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.
prereq_text: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.

subject: IBUS
title: /MGMT 457 Global Entrepreneurship
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Practical issues associated with taking small- and medium-size business global; includes importing and exporting, developing global strategies, evaluating market opportunities, regional impact on economies and people. Prerequisite: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School. Cross Listing: MGMT 457/IBUS 457 .
prereq_text: Admission to upper division in Mays Business School.

subject: IBUS
title: Latin American Markets
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Comparing and contrasting the Latin American, Canadian and U.S. markets across different variables, including culture, economics, social and legal aspects. May be repeated for credit if taken in a different country.

subject: IDIS
title: Introduction to Industrial Distribution
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Definition, history, types of industrial distribution; range of products; line of distribution; function of and services provided by distributors; distributor operational and financial analyses; measures of organizational effectiveness; employment and advancement opportunities in the field of industrial distribution.

subject: IDIS
title: Sales Engineering
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Sales and sales management techniques for analyzing distribution challenges and providing solutions through effective communication; establishing credibility, effective questioning techniques, developing solutions, presenting solutions, anticipating objections and gaining a commitment, plus techniques for building, developing and compensating an effective sales organization. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 or concurrent enrollment; industrial distribution major or technical sales minor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 or concurrent enrollment; industrial distribution major or technical sales minor.

subject: IDIS
title: Manufacturer Distributor Relations
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Approaches and procedures for developing and maintaining effective manufacturer distributor relations: marketing channel design, channel roles, managing uncertainty, legal and ethical imperatives, conflict resolution, decision support and strategic marketing. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 or concurrent enrollment; industrial distribution major or technical sales minor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 or concurrent enrollment; industrial distribution major or technical sales minor.

subject: IDIS
title: Distribution Logistics
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Study of concepts, issues and techniques used to plan, analyze and control the logistics network; examination of three key logistical decision-making areas: inventories, facilities and transportation; techniques and technologies for managing and optimizing the logistical (supply) chain. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; grade of C or better in STAT 201 , STAT 211 , or STAT 303 ; industrial distribution major.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; grade of C or better in STAT 201 , STAT 211 , or STAT 303 ; industrial distribution major.

subject: IDIS
title: Distributor Information and Control Systems
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Industrial distribution systems including hardware and software operations; inventory management, vendor evaluation; physical distribution systems; use of bar codes, radio frequency and other automated data entry techniques; purchasing operations. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; industrial distribution major, junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; industrial distribution major, junior or senior classification.

subject: IDIS
title: Distributor Financial Management
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Maximization of shareholder value; assessment and improvement of firm performance utilizing financial statement analysis and industry studies; methods for planning, implementing and monitoring profitability from distributor operations; procedures for controlling cash flow; credit and receivables, payables, inventory, capital assets, personnel and productivity; related financial operations. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; grade of C or better in ACCT 209 or ACCT 229 .
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 240 ; grade of C or better in ACCT 209 or ACCT 229 .

subject: IDIS
title: Industrial Distribution Technical Sales Seminar
description: Credit 1. 1 Other Hour. Practical applications for materials presented in academia; practical insights delivered by industry guest speakers from their perspectives of what they encounter and expect in the real-world of industrial distribution sales. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.
prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

subject: IDIS
title: Purchasing Applications in Distribution
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Applications of purchasing systems, specifically for the distribution industry; emphasis on supplier relations, strategic purchase planning, supplier evaluation, global purchasing techniques, cost analysis, life cycle costing, value analysis; case studies and procurement modeling for distributors. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 340 ; grade of C or better in IDIS 343 or concurrent enrollment; junior or senior classification in industrial distribution major.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 340 ; grade of C or better in IDIS 343 or concurrent enrollment; junior or senior classification in industrial distribution major.

subject: IDIS
title: Industrial Sales Force Development
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Techniques and processes for developing, maintaining and leading high performing industrial sales organizations; organization planning and forecasting processes, processes and procedures for identifying and developing talented sales professionals who can operate within a sales process and provide solutions to customers while growing profitable accounts. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in IDIS 330 ; senior classification in industrial distribution or technical sales minor.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 330 ; senior classification in industrial distribution or technical sales minor.

subject: IDIS
title: The Quality Process in Distribution
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Application of the Deming principles specifically for distributors, including customer needs analysis, research and data collection methodology, employee involvement techniques, team building, statistical methods and data analysis; solutions to quality problems for distributors, lean and six-sigma principles. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 ; senior classification in industrial distribution.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 ; senior classification in industrial distribution.

subject: IDIS
title: Distribution Project and Process Management
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Design and development of a solution to a distribution problem using systematic research methods and tools in a team-based environment; application of systems thinking to develop best practices related to the chosen field, logistics, operations, sales, etc., to determine the impact of their proposed solution on other components, or fields, of the business. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 ; grade of C or better in ESET 300 , IDIS 344 , and MMET 301 or concurrent enrollment; must be taken the long semester immediately prior to IDIS 444 ; senior classification in Industrial Distribution.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 ; grade of C or better in ESET 300 , IDIS 344 , and MMET 301 or concurrent enrollment; must be taken the long semester immediately prior to IDIS 444 ; senior classification in Industrial Distribution.

subject: IDIS
title: Distribution Project and Process Management II
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Continuation of IDIS 443 ; second-semester in capstone design sequence; design and development of a solution(s) to a distribution problem using systematic research methods and tools in a team-based environment; application of a systems-thinking approach for the development of best practices related to the chosen field such as logistics, operations, sales, etc. to determine the impact of their proposed solution on other component areas of the business. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 464 or IDIS 443 ; grade of C or better in IDIS 424 , IDIS 433 , IDIS 434 , and IDIS 450 , or concurrent enrollment; satisfactory grade in ENTC 399 or concurrent enrollment; must be taken in the last semester of coursework; senior classification in industrial distribution.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 464 or IDIS 443 ; grade of C or better in IDIS 424 , IDIS 433 , IDIS 434 , and IDIS 450 , or concurrent enrollment; satisfactory grade in ENTC 399 or concurrent enrollment; must be taken in the last semester of coursework; senior classification in industrial distribution.

subject: IDIS
title: Analytics for Distribution Operation
description: Credits 4. 3 Lecture Hours. 2 Lab Hours. Fundamental concepts in data analytics; transformation of business transaction data and visualization with state-of-the-art software; various statistical and analytical models used in the distribution world; building and interpreting the predictive analytics model for strategic and tactical decisions making problems. Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 and IDIS 344 ; senior classification in industrial distribution.
prereq_text: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 and IDIS 344 ; senior classification in industrial distribution.

subject: IDIS

description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in IDIS 343 and ACCT 209 or ACCT 229 ; grade of C or better in ESET 300 , IDIS 344 , and MMET 301 or concurrent enrollment; must be taken the long semester immediately prior to IDIS 444 ; senior classification in industrial distribution major.

title: Industrial Business to Business Marketing
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. subject: INST

description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. This course is intended to provide prospective teachers, and all undergraduate majors, with background information and insight to explore the historical, philosophical and societal foundations of education for all students. Course content is selected to align with the course description and the current state of scholarship in the field. The presentation of course content fosters critical thinking in the context of scholarly consensus and debate, rather than instructors’ views, values or beliefs; also taught at Qatar campus.

prereq_text: Junior or senior classification.

description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Basic principles of language acquisition, multiple approaches to second language acquisition; individual differences and second language acquisition; stages of second language development; multiple approaches to assessment. Prerequisite: INST or EDIS majors.

description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. subject: INTA
title: Professional Writing for Public Service
description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Development of essential communication skills tailored for the unique demands of public service careers; combination of traditional writing techniques with modern AI literacy to master strategies to craft impactful messages, manage collaborative projects, and optimize productivity; emphasis on practical application including writing and revision processes, enhanced by AI tools; crafting and organizing messages using analytic frameworks and the BLUF approach; editing for clarity, coherence, and impact; collaborating on team projects to produce high-quality deliverables; leveraging both foundational writing skills and cutting-edge AI capabilities. prereq_text: Grade of C or better in ENGL 104 ; admission to the BUSH school.

description: Credits 3. 3 Lecture Hours.
